system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: ALLHAT-LLT NCT00000542 - Antihypertensive and Lipid-Lowering Treatment to Prevent Heart Attack Trial (ALLHAT)
Investigational drug: pravastatin
Document: Pravastatin reduces restenosis after coronary angioplasty of high grade stenotic lesions: results of SHIPS (SHIga Pravastatin Study) (journal, published 1996-09-01, source pmid:8924063)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Pravastatin reduces restenosis after coronary angioplasty of high grade stenotic lesions: results of SHIPS (SHIga Pravastatin Study)

We conducted a multicenter prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to test whether pravastatin, a hydroxymethyl glutaryl coenzyme A reductase inhibitor, can decrease restenosis after percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA). Pravastatin 10 mg twice daily was begun at least 10 days prior to elective PTCA in patients with total cholesterol less than 280 mg/dl. The end-point was a between-group comparison of the frequency of restenosis defined as a more than 50% loss of the initial gain in diameter stenosis at the PTCA site at 3 months during follow-up by automated quantitative coronary arteriography. Of 207 patients randomly assigned to study groups, 139 patients underwent PTCA; 133 procedures were successful, and 124 patients underwent follow-up angiography at 3 months, and 179 lesions (85 pravastatin, 94 placebo) in 124 patients (62 pravastatin, 62 placebo) were analyzed. The two groups were comparable for baseline characteristics. Total cholesterol decreased by 19.6% in the pravastatin group (p < 0.001) but not in the placebo group. Although the restenosis rate was not different in the two groups (29.4% in pravastatin vs. 39.4% in placebo, p = 0.215) as a whole, it was reduced to about one fifth (8.8%) in the pravastatin group compared with 44.8% in the placebo group (p = 0.0011) when the comparison was restricted to high grade lesions (> or = 75% diameter stenosis, 34 lesions in pravastatin, 29 lesions in placebo). Pravastatin thus reduces restenosis after PTCA of high grade lesions.
--- END ---
